hero.subtitle: Studying Postgraduate Biomedical Engineering in France is a great option for students who want to combine engineering, biology, medicine and healthcare technology.

overview: \\Biomedical Engineering PG in France\\ is a great choice for students who want to develop technologies connecting engineering and health.
France offers specific training in medical imaging, nanomedicine, bioengineering, biomechanics and medical devices to its engineering schools and universities.

French Biomedical Engineering PG Eligibility Requirements French Biomedical Engineering PG Eligibility Requirements varies from program to program, university and year of admission. Applicants will generally be expected to have a relevant undergraduate qualification. The typical academic background is: - Bioengineering - Mechanical engineering - Electrical Engineering/Electronics - Electronics or Instrumentation - Bioengineering or Biotechnology - Physics/Applied Science - Other Engineering or Scientific related disciplines A bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification is normally required for a two-year national master's degree. Normally, entry to the second year will be on the basis of appropriate advanced study and adequate subject knowledge. Indian students should check the accepted undergraduate qualifications and subject requirements before applying for a \\Master's in Biomedical Engineering in France\. 5. French Biomedical Engineering PG Admission Requirements Most French universities and engineering schools assess candidates on the basis of academic suitability, technical knowledge and language proficiency. \\General Admission Requirements for Biomedical Engineering in France\\ are: Academic requirements: An accredited first-cycle qualification in a relevant discipline, with an appropriate background in mathematics, physics, biology, engineering or other subjects specified by the program. \\English language requirements:\\ Students taking English-taught courses may need to provide IELTS, TOEFL or other approved qualifications. The score required will vary depending on the institution, and some programs may accept other evidence of your English ability. \\French-language requirements:\\ Courses taught in French may require a recognized French language certificate. Requirements vary according to program and student profile. Additional selection criteria: Some institutions may review academic transcripts, statement of purpose, recommendation letters, interview, research experience, or technical projects.

sections.lead: \\Biomedical Engineering PG in France\\ is a great choice for students who want to develop technologies connecting engineering and health.

groups.text: \\Main advantages of biomedical engineering study in France:\\

items: \\Specialised education:\\ Access to engineering and life-science education, medical technology and healthcare innovation.
\\Research opportunities:\\ Work on medical devices, healthcare systems, biomedical research, and advanced technologies.
\\Industry exposure:\\ Projects and internships in research laboratories and health technology companies.
\\Advanced specialisations\\: Medical imaging, biomaterials, biomechanics, tissue engineering and nanomedicine.
\\Further study:\\ Options to undertake doctoral research or a PhD following a related postgraduate qualification.
\\European research networks:\\ Experience of research collaborations and technology networks in Europe.

The language of instruction is determined by the institution and the course. Students coming from abroad have to verify whether the \\Biomedical Engineering masters program in France\\ They chose to be taught in English, French or in both languages.

sections.title: Biomedical Engineering Courses in France
sections.lead: In France, \\postgraduate biomedical engineering courses\\ can be national master's degrees, engineering degrees, or specific courses in health care technology.

items: \\Biomedical Engineering in France\\ has popular specializations such as:
\\Medical Imaging and Image Processing:\\ Explore imaging systems, diagnostic technologies and biomedical signal analysis.
\\Nanomedicine:\\ Discover how nanotechnology can be used for diagnosis, treatment and drug delivery.
\\Medical Devices & Instrumentation:\\ Understand the design, development, testing and maintenance of medical equipment.
\\Biomechanics and Bioengineering:\\ The study of mechanical properties of biological systems, prosthetics, biomaterials and tissue engineering.
\\Biomedical Materials:\\ Find materials for medical implants and other health care applications.
\\Healthcare Technology Management:\\ Medical equipment management, quality assurance, safety and regulatory affairs.
Some of the pathways to the engineering degree are not aligned with the standard 2-year French national master's degree in terms of duration and admission structure.

sections.title: Recognition and Accreditation of Biomedical Engineering Programs in France
sections.lead: Before registering in a \\Biomedical Engineering postgraduate program in France\\students should verify the exact qualification granted by the institution.

items: In post-graduate French higher education, there are multiple types of qualifications:
\\National Master's Degree:\\ A master's degree recognized at national level within the French higher education system.
\\Engineering Diploma:\\ Issued by an accredited engineering school. Recognition will depend on the type of diploma and its accreditation.
\\Specialised Postgraduate Qualification:\\ A qualification that may not have the same status as a national master's degree.

Students who intend to work internationally should also take into account the requirements for professional recognition in their host country. Recognition of a degree does not automatically result in authorization to practice for all regulated health care or engineering professions.
Confirm before you accept an offer:
The awarding university and official degree title.
whether the program leads to a national master's degree, an engineering diploma or a specialization.
The institution's accreditation or recognition status.
The length and academic credit.
Requirements for recognition of work or study in the country you want to move to.

sections.title: Salary and Job Scope after Biomedical Engineering PG in France
sections.lead: \\Master's in Biomedical Engineering in France\\ can improve your career prospects in the medical technology, healthcare equipment, research, and product development industries.

items: Real job opportunities depend on the student's major, practical experience, language skills and the hiring market.
Possible jobs after Biomedical Engineering PG in France are:
Biomedical Engineer
Medical Device Design Engineer
Research and Development Engineer
Medical Imaging Engineer
Biomedical Instrumentation Engineer
Biomechanics or Biomaterials Engineer
Quality Assurance or Validation Engineer
Medical Device Regulatory Affairs Specialist
Clinical Engineering or Hospital Equipment Specialist
Biomedical Research Assistant or Doctoral Researcher

Employers include medical device manufacturers, health care technology companies, hospitals, research laboratories, biotechnology companies, and organizations engaged in product testing and regulatory compliance.
Salary Expectations Post Biomedical Engineering PG in France

Salaries vary by job role, location, employer, experience and qualification. Graduates should not assume that one salary figure applies to all but should look at current French job advertisements and salary surveys for similar posts.
Speaking French fluently can be a good way to get local jobs, especially if you are looking for work with hospitals, clients, healthcare providers or in regulatory communication.

faqs.q: Can an international student study Biomedical Engineering in France?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian students and other international applicants can apply to eligible French universities and engineering schools if they meet the programme's academic, language and application requirements.

faqs.q: Is Biomedical Engineering in English in France?
faqs.a: Some relevant programs or specializations are taught in English, others in French. The language of instruction for the program and the academic year concerned must be verified by the applicant.

faqs.q: What are the tuition fees for Biomedical Engineering PG in France?
faqs.a: Fees vary according to the institution and the qualification. The reference differentiated fee for non-EU students enrolled in covered national master's programs is €3,950 per year and the reference fee for covered engineering degree programs is €2,902 per year for 2026–2027. There may be some exceptions and some course specific fees.
